alternate_language_surface_label: Example State official voter-information alternate-language discovery policy
delivery_role_note: Separate locale URLs, hreflang reciprocity, generic-language and x-default fallback, and locale-adaptive crawl discipline shape whether search can send voters directly to the correct current official language variant.
fallback_policy_note: Unmatched languages land on a current selector/help page or generic-language page that still preserves the ordinary official office/help route rather than a decorative splash page.
partial_translation_boundary_note: Template-only or selected-content language paths are not advertised as full equivalent current translations in alternate-language clusters.
locale_adaptive_policy_note: If locale-adaptive delivery exists, the office still preserves stable locale URLs for current official translated equivalents and does not rely on IP or browser-language adaptation alone for discovery.
robots_consistency_note: Robots posture is reviewed across locale variants so translated equivalents are not silently less crawlable than the dominant-language page.
markup_language_note: HTML lang attributes and language-link annotations remain in place for accessibility and markup clarity even though search language detection does not depend only on hreflang or lang.
